reasons: The excerpt explicitly describes filters for click data and scroll depth, then the area feature, and explains that the latter dissects the percentage of people clicking different website elements.
The source directly frames heat-map and scroll-map analysis around identifying the desired core action, determining whether users reach or take it, and considering ways to move them toward it.

The observation and condition are supported, but the source only says empty-area clicks "might be something we want to investigate further." The action makes that tentative possibility an unconditional instruction once the condition occurs; retain the tentative qualifier.
The excerpt supports a tentative hypothesis that image clicks may reflect lack of platform understanding and that a video might be illustrated there.
The title adds that this is a video "to test," but the source does not propose a test, experiment, or validation procedure; it only offers a speculative design hypothesis.
The excerpt supports reviewing the 75%, 50%, and 25% scroll checkpoints and mentions an average-fold marker.
The source presents checkpoint review as what the speaker "typically" likes to examine. The action states it as an unqualified directive and should preserve that qualification.

The excerpt says the hero should communicate who the company is, what it does, and what is in it for the visitor, ideally within five seconds, and says failure to communicate this will typically lead to a large post-hero drop-off rather than a 93%–95% rate.

The source explicitly says the presenter clicks the homepage in the example walkthrough and distinguishes the two-page example account from the stated typical list of 5 to 10 popular pages segmented by traffic volume.

The supplied excerpt ends mid-sentence immediately after beginning a discussion of testimonials placed in the middle or at the bottom of a site. The candidate correctly limits itself to identifying that the point is incomplete.

The source identifies clicks around informational, non-clickable check marks as a potential area of enhancement. The candidate appropriately uses the qualified action "Consider" and does not invent a specific enhancement.
The source supports doing surveys and gathering feedback to understand what information matters to customers.

The asserted depends_on relation is not supported. The excerpt discusses customer research after introducing scroll checkpoints, but does not make reviewing those checkpoints a prerequisite for conducting surveys or obtaining feedback.
The candidate accurately reports these as examples and numerical claims made in the excerpt, including the cited review counts, ratings, trust claims, trial, and shipping offer.
It appropriately notes that the excerpt itself does not independently verify the external claims.
The excerpt supports examining the most-used navigation elements and main-navigation click locations.
The source describes this as what the speaker "typically" wants to look at. The action should preserve that qualification rather than present it as an unconditional instruction.

source_limitations: The excerpt begins mid-sentence and ends mid-sentence, so surrounding context and the conclusion of the testimonial-placement discussion are unavailable.
This appears to be a spoken walkthrough/transcript; some phrasing, product names, and numerical statements may be transcriptionally ambiguous.
Performance figures, review counts, ratings, and generalized conversion or scrolling benchmarks are asserted by the speaker in the excerpt but are not independently substantiated within it.

The excerpt provides only limited operational detail for several recommendations, including how to investigate anomalous clicks, choose among screenshot variants, conduct surveys, or validate a proposed video change.
